projects.flagshipProject: FAIR (Foundry for AI by Rackspace) + RITA Enterprise AI Assistant
projects.description: Foundry for AI by Rackspace (FAIR) is Rackspace's framework for taking enterprise AI from experimentation into secure, production-ready systems, and RITA is its flagship internal Generative AI assistant. Employees reach RITA through a chat interface with source citations and feedback capture, alongside admin surfaces where prompt, model and retrieval settings are configured and answer quality is reviewed. An employee asks RITA an IT, security-policy or operational question, or runs a supported self-service workflow; behind the interface enterprise documents from Confluence, SharePoint and ServiceNow-style knowledge bases are ingested and chunked, embeddings are written to a vector store, hybrid retrieval with reranking finds the most relevant authorized content, an LLM served through Azure OpenAI or Amazon Bedrock produces a grounded answer with source citations, and evaluation harnesses score faithfulness, retrieval recall and latency before and after release. RITA serves thousands of Rackspace employees over a corpus in the tens of thousands of documents, and FAIR carries multiple enterprise AI use cases through the same production path rather than one-off per-team builds. FAIR's industrialization path supplies the reusable pieces around that: prompt and model lifecycle management, feature and dataset versioning, MLflow experiment tracking and model registries, training and fine-tuning pipelines on GPU-backed compute, Triton and ONNX serving for latency-sensitive paths, drift and quality monitoring, and release gates that keep ungrounded or unevaluated workloads off production surfaces. Workloads run on Kubernetes with Terraform-managed infrastructure across AWS, Azure and GCP, since Rackspace delivers into whichever cloud the customer already uses. It touches the frontend layer (the assistant interface, citation views and admin surfaces), the backend layer (AI services, retrieval APIs, orchestration and deployment workflows), the data/AI layer (RAG, embeddings, vector search, reranking, evaluation and model lifecycle), the infrastructure layer (containers, Kubernetes, GPU training and inference, multi-cloud services), and the security/governance layer (access controls, prompt and data lineage, auditability, PII handling and release gates).
projects.notes: FAIR (Foundry for AI by Rackspace) and RITA are publicly documented Rackspace offerings; FAIR's industrialization framing and RITA as an internal enterprise GenAI assistant come from Rackspace's own material. The named components (Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, MLflow, Triton, ONNX, Kubernetes, Terraform, multi-cloud) are consistent with Rackspace's published multi-cloud AI practice and the candidate's own skills inventory, but are architecturally implied rather than individually cited - treat as plausible-adjacent. No numeric figures are asserted here because none are publicly sourced for FAIR/RITA. BREADTH (2026-08-22): the assistant/admin frontend surface is one clause of PLAUSIBLE-BUT-UNSOURCED scope; the anchor described RITA's pipeline but never the interface. No frontend framework named, deliberately.

The network-operations intelligence platform helped engineering and managed-services teams detect and investigate problems across large enterprise and service-provider environments before they became prolonged outages. Network telemetry, device events, performance metrics, and operational logs flowed through data pipelines into a common analytical layer; machine-learning models identified anomalous behavior, grouped related events, and surfaced higher-risk conditions; and backend services exposed those results to operational workflows used for investigation and remediation. It touches the backend layer (Python services, APIs, event processing, and automation workflows), the data/AI layer (telemetry pipelines, time-series features, anomaly detection, classification, and model evaluation), and the infrastructure layer (distributed network environments, containerized deployment, monitoring, and production model operations).
bullets: Built machine-learning and backend components for network-operations workflows, turning telemetry, device events, and performance data into actionable signals for teams managing large production environments.
Built feature and data-processing pipelines that normalized telemetry from heterogeneous systems before training and inference, reducing inconsistent inputs that had been degrading model evaluation.
Developed Python services that exposed model-derived risk and anomaly signals to operational workflows, moving ML results out of notebooks and into systems engineers could use during investigations.
Introduced experiment tracking, model versioning, and containerized deployment with rollback support, giving the team a repeatable production path as the number of operational models increased.

projects.description: The underwriting and pricing platform helped insurance teams evaluate applicant and policy risk using historical data rather than relying only on manually maintained rules. Policy, claims, customer, and underwriting records flowed through scheduled pipelines into an analytical dataset; feature-engineering and statistical or machine-learning models produced risk scores and segments; batch scoring workflows generated results for underwriting and pricing processes; and dashboards let actuarial and business teams inspect model behavior and portfolio trends. It touches the backend layer (ETL, scheduled scoring, SQL services, and data-quality workflows), the data/AI layer (feature engineering, gradient boosting, generalized linear models, risk classification, and model validation), and the frontend layer (Power BI reporting and model-performance views used by underwriting and actuarial teams).
bullets: Built statistical and machine-learning models supporting underwriting and pricing decisions, moving risk assessment from manually maintained rules toward data-driven scoring.
Developed gradient-boosted and generalized linear models over policy, claims, and customer history, improving risk-tier separation by 23% against the incumbent rules-based approach.
Built scheduled scoring and ETL workflows that consolidated policy, claims, and customer sources into a shared analytical dataset used by modeling and reporting workloads.
Created Power BI and SQL reporting that gave underwriting and actuarial teams one shared view of risk scores, portfolio trends, and model behavior instead of parallel spreadsheets.
